content.introduction: Fed officials expressed concerns about inflation, sparking discussions about a potential rate hike during their April meeting, the last chaired by Jerome Powell. The minutes indicated a growing number of policymakers believed a rate increase could be necessary if inflation stayed above target. This was the second consecutive meeting with increasing dissent on the need for a rate hike.

A majority of Federal Reserve officials warned the central bank would likely need to consider raising interest rates if inflation continued to run persistently above their 2% target, minutes of the April 28-29 Federal Open Market Committee meeting showed. Mike McKee reports.
